newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Qantas sees A$100 mln extra fuel costs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Qantas sees A$100 mln extra fuel costs.

text.p: Qantas Airways Ltd managing director James Strong said on Friday the rise in jet fuel prices is likely to add A$100 million to the airline's costs in the year to June 30, 1997.

"We estimate the higher fuel price to increase our costs this year by A$100 million," Strong told Australian Broadcasting Corp (ABC) radio. Qantas said on Thursday that the higher fuel price increased costs by A$50 million in the 1996/97 first half.
Strong also said Qantas aimed in the 1996/97 year to at least match the 1995/96 year's operating profit of A$401.4 million.
"We have said for the second half of this year that our target is to equal our profit last year," Strong said.

"Our total profit before tax was just over A$400 million last year and we are still striving to do that it won't be through growth in revenue, it will be through further tight control over costs," he said.
Qantas, which is 25 percent owned British Airways Plc, reported a 2.4 percent rise in net profit to A$151.6 million for the six months ended December 31, 1996.
The airline's share ended at a record close of A$2.54, up eight cents on active volume of 8.06 million, after earlier reaching a record high of A$2.57.
